mechanism: Both drugs possess anticholinergic and CNS depressant properties that may additive effects on cognition and urinary retention; tolterodine is metabolized by CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 while ethosuximide has minimal metabolism interactions but additive CNS effects are concerning.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (urinary retention, cognitive impairment) and CNS depression; consider alternative anticonvulsant if tolterodine effects become problematic.
